title: Grace acting on the mind
source_text: XXIV. Pagina vero sequenti ut actus gratiae divinae sigillatim exponant, observant tria in homine corrupto egere correctione & regeneratione, mentem, voluntatem, affectum, ac triplici huic subjecto gratiae divinae triplices actus accommodant. Primum ergo, ut ipsi sententiam suam exprimunt, Mentem Deus verbo & spiritus sui illuminatione de voluntate sua salutifera certiorem reddit, eamque ut assentiatur verbi veritati facit. Et quanquam homo possit vel per negligentiam, vel per malitiam voluntatis, hanc illuminationem & revelationem, tunc cum ea primitus vel externe, vel etiam interne menti fit, respuere, contemnere, nec eam alte in animum admittere, unde ignorantia affectata oritur; fieri tamen non potest ut si quando veritas clare & perspicue a Spiritu Sancto menti praesentetur, intellectus non assentiatur, aut judicium suspendat, sed ab objecto ita proposito, & a spiritu insinuato, determinatur ad assentiendum, nec potest intellectus ex se illi illuminationi resistere, cum ab objecto suo determinetur.
pass_a_gloss: XXIV. But on the following page to set out the acts of divine grace one by one, they observe that three things in corrupt man need correction & regeneration, the mind, the will, the affection, and to this threefold subject they fit threefold acts of divine grace. First then, as they themselves express their opinion, God by his word & the illumination of his spirit makes the mind more certain of his saving will, and makes it assent to the truth of the word. And although man can either through negligence, or through malice of the will, reject, despise this illumination & revelation, at the time when it is first made to the mind either externally, or even internally, nor admit it deep into the soul, whence affected ignorance arises; yet it cannot happen that if at any time the truth be clearly & plainly presented to the mind by the Holy Spirit, the intellect should not assent, or suspend judgment, but by the object so proposed, & by the spirit insinuated, it is determined to assent, nor can the intellect of itself resist that illumination, since it is determined by its object.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXIV. On the following page, to set out the acts of divine grace one at a time, they note that three things in corrupt man need correcting and regenerating: the mind, the will and the affections. To this threefold subject they match three kinds of act of divine grace.

First, in their own words: 'By his word and the enlightening of his Spirit, God assures the mind of his saving will and brings it to assent to the truth of the word. Through carelessness or through malice of will, a person can spurn and scorn this enlightening and revelation when it first comes to the mind, outwardly or even inwardly, and can refuse to take it deep into his soul, and from this comes affected ignorance.

Even so, once the truth is set clearly and plainly before the mind by the Holy Spirit, the intellect cannot fail to assent or hold back its judgment. It is determined to assent by the object so presented and by the Spirit who instils it, and the intellect cannot of itself resist that enlightening, since its object determines it.'
